notes.title: Rogue Planet has Re-Released on Itch.io!
notes.content:
Rogue Planet is finished and out on itch for you to play!

How far will you go to save yourself? 
And where will you run to forget what you've done?

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XGiuiEt5XWs

Game Download:
https://3vet.itch.io/rogue-planet-lines-of-dead-sand

How to play Rogue Planet:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BjNMefBh7yE

Featuring:

-Over 20 playable levels!

-HD Graphics and Lighting with HDR Support!

-A Cinematic and Otherworldly Soundtrack!

-A Minimal and Immersive HUD!

-Tons of Guns! 

-Secrets and Easter Eggs!

-A Branching Narrative with 7 Endings!

-A Realtime Graphics Menu!

-Level Title Cards!

-FOV Sliders for You and Your Viewmodel!

-Large Scale Skyboxes with Huge View Distances!

-Spooky Monsters and Hallucinations!

-Aggressive AI Soldiers with Dialogue who Love Rolling! (And rocking too!)

-4 Hours of Gameplay!

-Reshade Post Processing Effects!

-New About and Loading Menu Screens

-And an overall polished game that's fun to play! I loved it, squeezed it, and called it George.

Play Rogue Planet: Dead Sand for free now on itch.io!

MINIMUM SPECS:

OS: Windows 7, 8, 10, 11

Processor: Intel Dual-Core 2GHz or AMD Dual-Core 2GHz

Memory: 8 GB RAM

Graphics: Integrated Intel UHD 520 or AMD Ryzen Graphics equivalent

DirectX: Version 11

Storage: 6 GB available space

Sound Card: DirectX Compatible Sound Card with latest drivers

RECOMMENDED SPECS:

OS: Windows 10 1903

Processor: Intel Quad-Core (i5 2300) or AMD Octo-Core (FX 8150)

Memory: 8 GB RAM

Graphics: 4 GB AMD or 4 GB NVIDIA GPU

DirectX: Version 11

Storage: 6 GB available space

Sound Card: DirectX Compatible Sound Card with latest drivers

Additional Notes: Would also recommend a SSD or HDD cache to help with load times. An SSHD would also work. This game also works on Windows 11. Unsure of Windows XP and Vista, but apparently it is listed as supported on GameGuru's store page.

Some known issues and things to note are now included in a helpful file called "Hey! Read this!.txt If you have any issues running the game, please read that first before asking any questions or reporting any bugs or issues.

And thank you for checking out my game. It's been something I've wanted to do for almost my entire life. And now, it's finally out. Needless to say, it's been a long journey, but it's one I am happy with having taken. I hope you'll be happy as playing it as I was making it. 

Steam Version Update:

As for this old steam version, it is going to be abandoned. Unfortunately, after 2 weeks of attempting to publish the game on steam, I was unsuccessful, as I found out the parts of GameGuru which allowed for Steam publishing had been broken beyond repair as a result of my modifications to the engine. In all of the years I was testing the game, something I neglected was to ensure there were no issues when attempting to put this game on steam. 

However, the methods I have used to make this game are simply far too baked into the engine to undo now. And as a result of a lack of finer controls over the steam api and user interface of GameGuru, I had to cancel the Steam update, and opt for other platforms.

So I'm sorry to anyone who was expecting to be able to play this game on steam. As a result of this cancellation, I will be putting the game on itch, gamejolt, and a few other places if possible. I hope you can forgive me, and are able to understand. 

Rogue Planet was my first game that I used mainly to learn level and game design, and unfortunately, a rather expensive lesson to have to learn the hard way. I'll be moving to unreal engine 4 and trying to make a much better game on that engine, but until then, I hope you enjoy my game here on GameGuru and have fun.

There will be new videos about the game on my youtube channel, so check that out if you haven't already. You can find it on my website: https://threeofspades.weebly.com/ then look in the social media page, and you'll find it there.

If you have any questions, comments, or suggestions, you can find my discord on there too. So don't hesitate to reach out, otherwise I can't know what you think without you saying anything. I am always at least willing to hear fun game ideas out within reason.

Also been working on more awards, adding more music from the orchestra of eternity, fixing up some of the text, improving more visuals, and making more fun sound stuff, alongside the usual map making. I don't want to spoil the endings, so I won't be showing off the other new maps. But thankfully the game has made some excellent progress and is nearing completion. I haven't made too many updates lately since this is just a casual hobby I do for fun, and work, life, and the holidays have pre-occupied my time as of late.

My current plan is to try to launch a public stress test early next year, which will be used to see how well the game runs before everything is set in stone, plus to see if you can break it so i know what to fix. You are highly encouraged to play that stress test when it releases, as it will be available to everyone this time. So when that happens, go ahead and try to break my game if you can. if you can't, then that's good because it's working. So in other words, I can't fix any bugs if no one says anything about them. Or if the goblins decide to poop on you in the wrestling section and when their dead corpse crashes into the toilet, it crashes the game, in which case, that is intentional and will not be fixed.

So hopefully it all works, and after I get done with my game, I'll see about giving back to the people who still use this engine and want to make games that look like they came out in 2014 on windows 8 as opposed to 1990 on the Nintendo 64. Because it really deserves a lot better than what Lee Bamber and his animal farm have allowed it to become. And seeing how none of them care about making this easy, I'll be taking matters into my own hands to dig this engine out of the grave.

Turns out gameguru can do some crazy stuff without overwhelming first time game developers with coding and learning advanced college courses they'll never use when they eventually have to work another job at McDonald's, so I'd rather more people be able to also make fun fps games that look good without giving up the entire idea because no one cared to help them when they were desperate and wanted their money while giving them a half baked product. 

I guess we'll see how it goes from the stress test to release, but otherwise, I'll be busy with Christmas, and I hope you have happy holidays. Unless you don't celebrate the holidays, in which case, I hope you enjoyed this news update.

For more news and info, please visit my website:
[url=https://threeofspades.weebly.com/]https://threeofspades.weebly.com/[/url]

I will also be uploading more Rogue Planet videos on the 3ofSpades Purgatory YouTube channel, so check that out too if you haven't already. Also been quiet on that because of life, but I won't be for much longer:

And yes, as you may have seen, Gary got an upgrade. Here is a sneak peek in level 2:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41243279/41347ad16f7c28c9efadc9e050e0bcee26fea055.png[/img]

I've gone through the effort of sharpening many various textures of a lot of the GameGuru models, mostly being the ones of models you will be constantly seeing throughout my game. Naturally models like the low poly cityscapes of the background aren't really in need of that when they're in the skybox 3 miles away. However, models like the trees, walls, buildings, and the enemies are. So while every model may not get this treatment, the focus should help many in game models and assets look better and more detailed while maintaining their original resolution as to not increase the requirements for those on lower end hardware.

While I was poking through the textures of a lot of models, I was running a few experiments and found I was able to improve the shading and details of many of the textures in GameGuru by opening the .dds texture files of a model, increasing the sharpness of the color and normal maps, or other texture maps, if the models even had any (which in my testing, 9/10 models did not even have a basic ambient occlusion, specular, or metallic map, which leads to some models looking better than others in the engine due to the unfinished PBR support.)

Most of what I found out about the various models and the textures on them was rather interesting. The actual textures were either taken from real life photos, presumably on a camcorder due to the very low resolution, and very haphazardly wrapped around the various low poly models, leading to the typical issue of most gameguru games where everything looks like moldy mashed potatoes and 144p YouTube videos from 2006, and/or exported to an incredibly blurred resolution that looked like someone smeared grease on them. I was able to fix them by pressing four buttons in Paint .net and got these results. 

So hopefully one of their updates that take 7 months to fix 1 bug can take some notes so games on this engine look more like windows 8 instead of XP. 

The Devil is in the Details, GameGuru. You know you don't deserve me. ːujelː

Anyways, enough of that.
More coming soon, take care and stay tuned!

notes.title: Demo 5 is Out Now!
notes.content:
Rogue Planet Demo 5 is out now! Play Free on itch.io! 
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ucCnye-YEOI

Itch.io Page:
[url=https://3vet.itch.io/rogue-planet-demo-5]https://3vet.itch.io/rogue-planet-demo-5[/url]

This is Rogue Planet: Consolidation Demo 5

Surreal Action Horror!

Rogue Planet Demo 5 is a standalone expansion to the original Steam release, set 2 years after the original. The climactic finale and final chapter of the first game taking place during the end of the world in 2012. Rogue Planet: Consolidation is a solo developed dreamlike FPS game made by 3ofSpades over the course of 6 years. It takes influences from LucasArts' games in their later years and late generation Xbox 360 and Playstation 3 games.

It is designed to push the GameGuru Engine to its limits with beautiful Graphics and satisfying Gameplay systems, while being accessible to lower end systems and taking minimal storage space.

The Story:

Now that you've awoken from the events of the original, you return to the places you once explored in your dreams to find answers.

Taking a job to repair a radar array leads to the place of origin to everything, as the truth of what happened in Santa Fe 2 years ago is finally beginning to unravel. Your interpretation of the truth will affect the world around you, and more importantly, the people living in it.

Be careful. Imaginations can be powerful things...

Do you think you can bring yourself to find the real truth one last time? No choice without a consequence, no consequence without a step taken.  With every step you take, there is a price to pay.

How far will you go to save yourself?

Featuring:

-7 new levels (Now Including New Poop Wrestling Easter Egg Levels! Yes, literally!)

-Remade lighting with HDR support and fixes

-New music

-New Hud

-8 new weapons

-New Secrets and Easter Eggs

-Audio Rebalancing

-New FPS Arms

-Fixed Ambient Occlusion

-New Level Title Cards

-FOV Fixes (Now you can properly adjust your FOV and your viewmodel!)

-Optimized View Distance and Removed Cluttered and Unused Models on Every Level

-New and Improved Hallucinations

notes.title: 7 Years Later!
notes.content:
Fun fact, this little game of mine has been in the making for about 7 years. I think the first ever build I made was on 4/20/2017. Time sure flies when you're having fun. So speaking of, it has been a while and I have a lot of new screenshots from an upcoming beta that's under active development.

If you are interested in the game, or perhaps have any suggestions for content you would like to see added, now would be a good time to leave your ideas in the discussions.

Some suggestions I'm currently developing: In-game achievements I'm calling "Awards" that way they work on both itch and Steam versions of the game, ambient occlusion fixes, an overhaul to the lumbermill investigation (as seen below), a tutorial for the various menus, some texture fixes for a few blurry models, a voice acting overhaul. 

A few things I've already finished include: An improved hud, new first person arm textures, and better organization for the various chapter cards, alongside optimizing the game and making sure it works and looks good. 

I am also planning on removing the stamina system and just giving you infinite sprint like it used to be but making the speed slower since the engine needs more time to load all the cool stuff.

Turned out no one got the memo that if you run 500 miles in the game without a break or two, you can get pretty tired, so no biggie, just thought it was a neat idea for this action horror game but apparently not. So go wild!

Anyways, I hope you enjoy my presentation! Take care!
